# `valueConfigs`: the dropdown value configs

Part of [generated data](../generated-data.md). `makeValueConfigs` must keep its `const` type parameter (the rule: [`src/01_SpreadsheetSchema/AGENTS.md`](../../src/01_SpreadsheetSchema/AGENTS.md)).

## How `valueConfigs` is generated

**`valueConfigs`** (`generated/valueConfigs.ts`) — generated by `ValueConfigOperator` (`05_Operators`) from the **value sources** in use, once `columnConfigs` is already synced. It asks Column Config for the distinct value sources its dropdown columns name and emits one entry per source under its value name. A Name or ID source is a live reference (below); every other source column is fetched in full on its own Table and becomes a fixed list: blanks are dropped, duplicates collapse to their first position, and sheet order is kept. A source column with a declared value name types every member (`number` and `date` give numbers, `checkbox` booleans, `string` strings), while an untyped source keeps each member's own primitive. A value name equal to a framework value name, or taken by two different sources, fails the config sync, naming both. **`makeValueConfigs` takes a `const` type parameter, and must keep it** (#18): without it the generated member lists infer as `string[]` and every dropdown column's value type collapses to bare `string`, which silently removes the union a switch over a Value Config's members is meant to be exhaustive against. The generated file carries no `as const` of its own, so the constructor is the only thing holding the literals. Measured at ~41k instantiations — see [type-check cost](../architecture/type-check-cost.md).

## The two kinds

Each entry is one of two kinds, and the value type and value schema of every column naming it follow the kind (#145):

- **A fixed list** is an array of members, each a string, number or boolean. The `const` parameter keeps it a literal tuple, so its value type is the union of its members, a number member staying a number literal, and its wire type is the union of their primitive kinds. Its value schema accepts only a member, and its default is its first member.
- **A live reference** is the marker `{ "kind": "liveReference" }`, with no members, because its options are rows added after the build. Its value type is `string`, and it takes the framework `string` value schema: any string is accepted, and its default is blank, so the column's **Empty value allowed** decides whether that blank reads. It never takes the `id` value schema, whose default throws.

Value Config is still on the config-sheet floor; as a Let api access Table it is one more value source, so its value names are `valueConfig<Header>`. The framework's `valueKinds/` test program installs a hand-written config set with one of each.

## Which sources are live

A source is a live reference when its header is its Table's Name header or ID header, as `tableLayout` declares them, whatever the column's type menu says (#147). Those columns identify the Table's rows, so the dropdown's options are the rows themselves: a row added there is an option at once, with no config sync, where a fixed list would hold only the rows of the last sync. Its source column isn't fetched. Its value name follows the rule for any source, so `unit[Name]` gives `unitName` and `unit[ID]` gives `unitId`, never the `id` value name. Nothing checks at read time that a reference names an existing row: a name with no match is the endpoint's to report.
